title: Ballari iron ore mining: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Iron ore mining turns a leased, finite resource into cash through a simple chain: extract, crush and screen, then move by road and rail to steel plants and traders.** Value sits in the mining lease and the environmental clearance, not in the plant; the crusher and washing units are modest capex, but the lease premium, royalty and statutory dues are the real cash sinks. **So when a proposal lands, check the lease deed, the approved mining capacity and the EC validity first; if any of the three is unclear, ask for the sanctioned lease order and the latest EC compliance return before you look at anything else.**

## Where cash sits and what has changed
**Working capital is short and self-funding in a good year: ore is sold largely on advance or near-cash terms, so the cycle is inventory at the stockyard plus receivables from steel buyers.** Peer results show the price side is soft — SMIORE's average realisation fell 17% y-o-y to INR 3,095/t in Q1FY'27 [7], though it rose 9% q-o-q on a recovery in domestic benchmark prices [6]. **Locally, the news is worse: the Supreme Court-appointed committee has been urged to visit mining-affected areas in Ballari and Chitradurga and report to the court before the next hearing [2].** That is a live regulatory overhang on leases and clearances, and it is the single fact that should shape your stance this quarter.

## The growth opportunity
**The demand pull is real and local: a 6 million tonne per annum steel plant with an 893 MW captive power plant has received environmental clearance in Ballari [1], and NMDC expects FY'27 output of around 60 million tonnes nationally [4].** Pursue established merchant miners with valid leases and a track record of statutory compliance, and the service layer around them — ore handling, crushing and transport contractors with written offtake. **Avoid new entrants whose only asset is an allotted lease with no EC, and avoid borrowers whose receivables depend on a single steel buyer.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the lease, not the balance sheet: keep tenor inside the lease and EC validity, take the mining lease and offtake assignment where legally possible, and set a debt-service cover covenant tested quarterly.** Take a monthly stock-and-sales statement, royalty and statutory-dues payment proof, and the EC compliance status every month. **If royalty or statutory dues slip by even one month, treat it as a cash-flow signal and ask for the bank statement the same week.**

## Early-warning signs
- **Lease or EC status (monthly):** any show-cause, suspension or court direction -> freeze fresh disbursement and review the account.
- **Realisation per tonne (monthly):** a fall beyond the peer range of INR 3,095/t [7] -> re-run the cash-flow and ask for the buyer-wise price list.
- **Statutory dues (monthly):** any delay in royalty or DMG payments -> ask for the bank statement and tighten the stock limit.
- **Buyer concentration (quarterly):** one buyer above half of sales -> seek an offtake agreement or reduce exposure.
